content: what are the steps involving in CPT?

assistant: The steps involved in the Curricular Practical Training (CPT) process are as follows:

1. **Request CPT**: The student initiates the process by requesting CPT through the school's established procedures.

2. **Review and Determine Eligibility**: The Designated School Official (DSO) reviews the request and determines if the student meets the eligibility criteria for CPT.

3. **Authorize CPT in SEVIS**: The DSO authorizes the CPT in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) for a specific employer.

4. **Print and Sign Form I-20**: The DSO prints and signs the Form I-20 document with the CPT authorization.

5. **Begin Work**: The student can start working on or after the CPT start date indicated on the Form I-20.

I'm in my first semester, am I still eligible ?

Assistant: Absolutely, you're on the right track! As an F-1 student, you can engage in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) after completing one full academic year and being lawfully enrolled on a full-time basis at an approved ICE SEVP-certified school. Since you're in your first semester, you're still eligible to apply for CPT once you've completed the required academic year. Remember, CPT must be an integral part of your established curriculum and can be either part-time or full-time. It's also worth noting that if you receive one year or more of full-time CPT, you'll become ineligible for Post-Completion OPT at the same educational level. So, make sure to discuss your options with your Designated School Official (DSO) to ensure you're prepared for any future opportunities.
